title: Compact audit payloads for RBAC activity with provenance and delta summarization
creator: Evelyn Cho
description: Design and implement a compact, queryable audit payload shape for RBAC v2 and admin operations that preserves provenance, supports efficient diff storage for target objects, and minimizes PII exposure. This ticket covers the payload contract, change-set encoding rules, indexing keys for lookups, redaction/hashing rules for sensitive fields, sampling policy for high-volume systems, and migration guidance for existing audit consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Audit envelope includes stable identifiers (event_id, trace_id, tenant_id, request_id) and canonical actor metadata (actor_id, actor_type, auth_method, session_id)
Target change-set encoded as a compact operation list (op, path, value_hash | value_preview) with a single-line human-readable summary field
Pre/post snapshots optional and gated by retention_policy and data_class (full only for admin-level changes, sampled for high-volume events)
PII redaction/hashing rules applied consistently with KMS-backed salts; hashed values are reversible only via internal tooling when allowed
Schema versioning header (audit_schema_v) and migration notes included; consumers can fall back to older schema versions via compatibility flag
Documented query patterns (by actor_id, target_id, action, timeframe, change-path) perform within SLO in staging benchmarks
Integration tests and a migration compatibility shim exist for at least three downstream consumers (console, billing, incident-runbook)
Security review signoff from Compliance before release
tasks: Create canonical audit envelope spec and wireframe (PRD link in comments)
Define op-set for diffs: add/remove/replace/rename/metadata-update and field path normalization rules
Implement server-side diff-generator for RBAC objects and admin changes
Add redact/hash pipeline step with KMS salt rotation support
Indexing plan: primary indices for (tenant_id, target_type, target_id), secondary for (actor_id, action, timeframe)
Benchmark storage and query cost under realistic traffic (simulate 1M events/day)
Add migration shim that emits v1/v2 envelopes for 30 days post rollout
comments: 2025-03-20 - Evelyn Cho: Kickoff. Attached initial PRD draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Payload+Revamp. Goal is to reduce audit storage by ~3x for high-volume admin ops while keeping forensic fidelity.
2025-03-21 - Carlos Mendes: Suggest we standardize on RFC 6902-like ops but avoid full JSON Patch; we'll use a compact op tuple to reduce payload size. Will prototype serializer.

2025-03-23 - Aisha Patel: Initial serializer prototype (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7192) produces op tuples: ["add", "/roles/3/members", "u:e4f2..."] and value_preview is base64 of first 64 bytes. Need feedback on value_preview semantics.

2025-03-24 - Priya Nair (Compliance): Confirmed KMS-backed salted hashing approach acceptable for PII; requirement to include hash_salt_version in envelope. Also requested a reversible-only-via-console flag for legal requests.

2025-03-25 - Design review (Liam O'Connor): Console UI will display human_summary and limited preview; expanding to full pre/post will require elevated roles. UI mockups stored at: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-audit-ui

2025-03-26 - SRE (Monica Ruiz): Storage sizing note: compact ops reduce average event size from 2.1KB to 0.8KB in our generator tests. Query plans require an append-only time-partitioned store with a small secondary index for actor lookups. We'll put a canary of 10% traffic to the new pipeline.

2025-03-27 - Aisha Patel: Merged serializer prototype branch into internal/integration for staging trial. Next: implement sampling policy and migration shim. Blocker: need approval for adding session_id to envelope (privacy review).
